cases.question: What happens when an invoice price is higher than the purchase order price, and who must resolve it and by when?
cases.answer: When the difference between the invoice price and the purchase order price exceeds 2% or €100, the invoice is blocked for payment with a price block. [2] The buyer responsible for the purchase order must resolve the price block within 10 business days. [1] The buyer resolves the price block either by correcting the purchase order price when the invoiced price is contractually valid and approved, or by asking the supplier for a credit note or a corrected invoice. [1] A buyer must never change a purchase order price only to release an invoice without a valid price agreement. [1]

cases.question: What are the lockout/tagout steps, and who is allowed to remove a padlock?
cases.answer: The first lockout step is to prepare the intervention by identifying all energy sources with the LOTO sheet and informing concerned operators. [2] The second step is to stop the machine using its normal controls. [2] The third step is to isolate every energy source including electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, mechanical, thermal, and chemical. [2] The fourth step is to apply a personal padlock and a tag with your name and date on each isolation point. [2] The fifth step is to release or block stored energy by bleeding pressure, blocking moving parts, and letting hot parts cool down. [2] The sixth step is to verify the absence of energy by trying to start the machine with normal controls and checking for voltage with a tester. [2] Only the person who applied a padlock may remove it. [1] A padlock left by an absent person can be removed with the written authorisation of the Maintenance Manager after trying to contact the person, checking that the machine can be restarted safely, and using the lock removal form. [1]

cases.question: How is a supplier's monthly score calculated, and what happens to a supplier that stays in class C?
cases.answer: Each supplier receives a monthly scorecard with a score from 0 to 100. [2] The monthly score is weighted 40% on delivery, 40% on quality, 10% on responsiveness and 10% on document compliance. [2] A supplier that stays in class C is required to have a corrective action plan within 30 days and a monthly review meeting. [1] If a supplier stays in class C for 3 consecutive months, it is placed on "new business hold", meaning no new parts or contracts are awarded to it. [1] When a supplier stays in class C for 3 consecutive months, the Sourcing Committee evaluates its phase-out. [1]

cases.answer: Every new supplier must provide a company registration extract less than 3 months old. [2] New suppliers must provide their VAT number, validated against the official register. [2] New suppliers must provide bank details on company letterhead, signed by an authorised representative. [2] New suppliers must provide a signed acknowledgement of the Supplier Code of Conduct (NX-PUR-006). [2] New suppliers must provide a general liability insurance certificate with cover of at least €2 million per claim. [2] New suppliers must provide a completed supplier information form covering contacts, ownership, and main sites. [2] The target onboarding lead time for an indirect supplier is 10 business days from the receipt of a complete file. [1]

cases.question: What is the procedure to approve a purchase request of more than €50,000?
cases.answer: For purchase requests from €50,000 to €249,999, the required approvers are the Site Director and the Category Manager. [1] The ERP workflow routes the request to the matching approvers automatically in the order shown in the table. [1] To create the requisition, describe the need, quantity, and estimated total value excluding VAT over the full contract duration in the ERP, select the cost center, and attach the required sourcing evidence. [2] For requests from €50,000, you must attach the bid comparison approved by the Category Manager in addition to at least three written quotes. [2] Each approver must approve or reject the requisition in the ERP within 3 business days. [2] If no action is taken, an automatic reminder is sent after 3 business days, and the requisition is escalated to the approver's line manager after 5 business days. [2] If the purchase involves machinery, equipment, tooling, or other capital assets, an approved capital expenditure request from the Investment Committee is required before creating the purchase requisition. [4]

cases.question: Quelle est la procédure pour valider une demande d'achat supérieure à 50 000 € ?

[3] Chaque approbateur doit approuver ou rejeter la demande dans l'ERP dans un délai de 3 jours ouvrés. [3] Un rappel automatique est envoyé après 3 jours ouvrés et la demande est escaladée vers le supérieur hiérarchique de l'approbateur après 5 jours ouvrés sans action. [3]

cases.question: What happens when an invoice price is higher than the purchase order price, and who must resolve it and by when?
cases.answer: When the difference between the invoice price and the purchase order price exceeds 2% and €100, the invoice is blocked for payment. [4] The buyer responsible for the purchase order must resolve the price block. [1] The price block must be resolved within 10 business days. [1] The buyer resolves it either by correcting the purchase order price when the invoiced price is contractually valid and approved, or by asking the supplier for a credit note or a corrected invoice. [1] A buyer must never change a purchase order price only to release an invoice without a valid price agreement. [1]

cases.question: How is a supplier's monthly score calculated, and what happens to a supplier that stays in class C?
cases.answer: Each supplier receives a monthly score from 0 to 100 on their monthly scorecard. [2] The monthly score is weighted 40% on delivery, 40% on quality, 10% on responsiveness, and 10% on document compliance. [2] A score below 70 places a supplier in class C, which requires a corrective action plan within 30 days and a monthly review meeting. [1] A supplier that stays in class C for 3 consecutive months is placed on "new business hold", meaning no new parts or contracts are awarded to it. [1] When a supplier is placed on new business hold or is in class C, its parts are inspected at 100% until Quality decides otherwise. [4] When a supplier stays in class C for 3 consecutive months, the Sourcing Committee also evaluates its phase-out. [1]

cases.question: What is the procedure to approve a purchase request of more than €50,000?
cases.answer: For purchase requests from €50,000 to €249,999, the required approvers are the Site Director and Category Manager. [3] The ERP workflow automatically routes the request to the required approvers in the order shown in the approval matrix. [3] The requester must create the requisition in the ERP, describe the need, quantity, and estimated total value excluding VAT over the full contract duration, and select the cost center. [5] The requisition must include the required sourcing evidence, including at least three written quotes and the bid comparison approved by the Category Manager. [5] Each approver must approve or reject the requisition in the ERP within 3 business days. [5] An automatic reminder is sent after 3 business days, and the requisition is escalated to the approver's line manager after 5 business days without action. [5]

cases.question: Quelle est la procédure pour valider une demande d'achat supérieure à 50 000 € ?
cases.answer: Créer la demande dans l'ERP en décrivant le besoin, la quantité, la valeur totale estimée hors TVA sur toute la durée du contrat et en sélectionnant le centre de coûts. [5] Joindre les éléments de sourcing requis à partir de 50 000 €, incluant le comparatif d'offres approuvé par le Category Manager. [5] Soumettre la demande pour qu'elle soit acheminée automatiquement par l'ERP vers les approbateurs de la tranche correspondante. [5] Chaque approbateur doit approuver ou rejeter la demande dans l'ERP dans un délai de 3 jours ouvrés. [5]
